slides.text: Anthropic Dispatch Anthropic Dispatch - remote access to Claude Cowork on MacOS from mobile claude app on your phone Need to update Cowork and App, and pair them using QR Code This remote access acts similar to OpenClaw, but more secure It is currently in "research preview" for Pro & Max subscribers Examples of tasks: organizing files, preparing documents, searching folders, running long background tasks -  essentially anything Claude Cowork can do on your desktop Claude Cowork runs each project inside a Linux virtual machine (VM) launched on your Mac Claude isn't operating directly on your file system -  it works inside that isolated VM with access only to folders and tools you explicitly grant Inside the VM, there's a second layer of protection using OS-level tools (bubblewrap + seccomp) that further restrict what processes can do https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13947068-assign-tasks-to-claude-from-anywhere-in-cowork Mamba-3 open-source State Space Model (SSM) Released by researchers fr omPrinceton 1.5B params, good accuracy and high performance at smaller size https://goombalab.github.io/blog/2026/mamba3-part1/ OpenAI GPT-5.4 nano Small, high-volume, cost efficient, via API only Context in 400K, out 128K tokens Knowledge cutoff: August 31, 2025 ​Text + image input; text output ​Pricing $0.2 / $1.25 (in/out) Anthropic vs Pentagon February - Anthropic was labeled as "supply chain risk" March 9 - Anthropic filed a lawsuit in federal court in CA March 17 - gov. filed a response asking to dismiss this lawsuit March 24 - preliminary injunction hearing

slides.title: OpenClaw uses CDP (Chrome DevTools Protocol) as the
slides.text: OpenClaw uses CDP (Chrome DevTools Protocol) as the core mechanism for browser control The key feature is the OpenClaw Browser Relay, a lightweight Chrome extension available on the Chrome Web Store. When you click it on any tab, it installs a local relay server on your machine that exposes a controlled WebSocket API to communicate with Chrome This relay forwards CDP commands between OpenClaw and your actual browser tab, including all your existing logged-in sessions OpenClaw uses Playwright on top of CDP for advanced actions The internal flow is: https://docs.openclaw.ai/tools/browser A small control server accepts HTTP requests from the AI agent It connects to Chromium-based browsers (Chrome, Brave, Edge) via CDP; Playwright is layered on top of CDP for actions like click, type, snapshot, PDF export; If Playwright is unavailable, only basic non-Playwright CDP operations run OpenClaw exposes three distinct modes, each using CDP differently: Extension Relay (port 18792) OpenClaw-Managed (port 18800) Remote CDP - Connects to a remote Chromium via cdpUrl Once connected, the agent interacts with the browser using snapshot-based element referencing OpenClaw Uses CDP

slides.text: Tandem - free, open-source browser for OpenClaw Designed from the ground up for human + AI agent collaboration, https://github.com/hydro13/tandem-browser https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ByQWanSmIQU https://x.com/steipete/status/2033451685352481214 Tandem provides a 250-endpoint local API covering tabs, navigation, page snapshots, sessions, DevTools, network mocking, and controlled automation - all purpose-built for agentic workflows It also has a 6-layer security model that accounts for the fact that an AI has live access to web content, and it keeps the human in the loop at ambiguous or risky decision points with explicit handoff moments instead of silent automation Research mode - OpenClaw can open multiple tabs, read pages, and summarize them while you work in the background HTML analysis - the agent can inspect the page structure Logged-in sessions - you authenticate inside Tandem and grant OpenClaw access to those accounts Human-in-the-loop - OpenClaw can pause and ask you to confirm before taking risky actions Wingman panel - a chat interface connecting OpenClaw directly to your browser session Everything runs on your own machine Tandem - Browser for OpenClaw

slides.title: Matt Berman - 14 OpenClaw use cases and
slides.text: Matt Berman - 14 OpenClaw use cases and best practices https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M-3w1wEv0M0 Use threaded conversations through Telegram to improve AI memory and context by separating topics into dedicated chat threads Use different AI models for specific tasks rather than one model for everything Delegate frequently to sub-agents to avoid blocking the main agent Implement multi-layered security measures against prompt injection Schedule automated cron jobs for routine tasks Use logging and documentation for debugging Regular system updates Use subscription services instead of APIs for cost savings Proper backup strategies with Git and cloud storage Write comprehensive tests Batch notifications to reduce distractions Use voice memo functionality for hands-free interaction Use here.now for publishing AI-generated content OpenClaw - Best Practices Use executable CLI commands or scripts instead of textual skills to save tokens where possible Claude Code instead of OpenClaw https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ODKMmKCgrvw Breaks agents into four zones: triggers (what activates the agent), context (system prompts and memory), tools (capabilities for interacting with systems), output (where work is stored) Example: email agent - connects via Telegram, fetches Gmail messages, and provides email summaries Claude Code is cheaper, more controllable, and transparent compared to OpenClaw, while maintaining full programmability and using Claude Max tokens instead of expensive alternatives

slides.title: OpenClaw Security Problems are NOT Solved. Here is
slides.text: OpenClaw Security Problems are NOT Solved. Here is an example of the problem: An attacker embeds a single instruction inside a forwarded email An OpenClaw agent summarizes that email as part of a normal task The hidden instruction tells the agent to forward credentials to an external endpoint The agent complies - through a sanctioned API call, using its own OAuth tokens The firewall logs HTTP 200. EDR records a normal process No signature fires. Nothing went wrong by any definition your security stack understands The six tools released in last 2 weeks have closed some gaps but left the three most critical attack surfaces wide open: No tool in existence monitors why an agent made a decision or what it chose to do with legitimate access. The attack lives in meaning, not code, so every binary-based defense is blind to it No tool currently provides cross-agent context isolation. This is the hard gap to close because it is tied to prompt injection - a systemic vulnerability affecting every LLM-powered agent system in the industry, not just OpenClaw There is still zero mutual authentication between agents delegating tasks to each other. If one agent gets compromised - the entire system gets compromised OpenClaw Security Problems are NOT Solved What a Real Solution Requires? Every skill should declare explicit permissions before execution, treating skills like mobile app installs rather than arbitrary text. This is the most concrete near-term step Deep architectural changes - Cross-agent context leakage cannot be patched; it requires rethinking how untrusted multi-agent memory and prompting are handled at the architecture level All security evaluation tools lack ability to do semantic monitoring. A new class of defense tooling needed.

slides.title: AI Updates Genspark Claw - "AI employee" Executes
slides.text: AI Updates Genspark Claw - "AI employee" Executes multi-step tasks end to end, not just generates drafts It runs inside a dedicated Genspark Cloud Computer per user, ensuring privacy through isolation You assign tasks via a simple message on WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, or Teams, and Claw handles research, drafting, scheduling, email, calls, and code deployment - then returns finished results It orchestrates over 70 AI models, including Claude Opus, GPT, and NVIDIA Nemotron Part of AI Workspace 3.0, it launched alongside Workflows, Meeting Bots, a Chrome Extension, and voice tools Genspark has reached $200M ARR and a $1.6B valuation Auto Research Claw Free, open-source (MIT) AI tool generating research paper Works with OpenClaw, runs a 23-stage, 8-phase research pipeline that searches real academic sources, screens them for quality, designs and runs Python experiments in a sandbox, and has multiple AI agents debate hypotheses and findings It features 4-layer citation integrity to minimize hallucinations and produces a complete formatted paper (5K - 6K words) in 1 hr The system is self-learning, extracting lessons from each run stored with a 30-day time decay, and supports scheduled recurring reports AI employees - autonomous agents that work 24/7 without constant prompting Unlike basic chatbots or even AI agents, AI employees follow a Standard Operating Procedure, run on a schedule, and control a dedicated computer with access to custom tools and databases Example of AI employees: strategy, sales, content, marketing, and personal/admin. Controlled via Telegram, each with a defined memory, skillset, and personality Hardware can be a dedicated PC, Mac Mini, or cloud VPS OpenClaw is a reasonable choice The key to success is : writing detailed SOPs (Standard Operating Procedure, a detailed, step-by-step written guide explaining exactly how to perform a specific task or process) using cron job scheduling for proactive task execution building custom API-connected tools This allows to reduce your manual workload from 100% down to roughly 20%. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XtzykHbS3kM Improving skills using "Auto Research (Karpathy)": https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qKU-e0x2EmE https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wQ0duoTeAAU

slides.title: OpenClaw Builds Million Dollar Business Building a Million
slides.text: OpenClaw Builds Million Dollar Business Building a Million Dollar Zero Human Company with OpenClaw - by Nat Eliason - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vF3dK1TywAk Experiment creating a "zero human company" using an AI agent named Felix built on OpenClaw. Felix has generated $80,000 in revenue over about a month through four main products: an info PDF, a marketplace called ClawArt for AI skills, custom AI employee services, and various earnings. The company operates with Felix as CEO and two other AI agents handling support and sales, with total operating costs around $400-500 monthly for AI subscriptions. Eliason emphasizes he maintains a hands-off approach as an advisor while working full-time elsewhere, only providing guidance rather than day-to-day management. He addresses AI doom concerns by arguing that while the technology could theoretically replace many knowledge workers, actual market adoption will be much slower than anticipated. The conversation explores broader implications of AI agents as personal assistants and business tools, with Eliason recommending people start simple with tools like Claude before advancing to more complex systems like OpenClaw. Use OpenClaw to Make $50K/Month https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w98X0ayMmF8 basic setup services ($500-5000 one time) ongoing AI system management (monthly recurrent) premium business transformation consulting ($10K-20K) Success comes from understanding business problems rather than technical expertise Become a trusted AI Strategist for Business https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6o9D9XLmVVg 1. conducting an AI audit to understand the business 2. creating a strategic roadmap 3. implementing solutions (often through contractors) 4. maintaining an ongoing partnership for recurring revenue That businesses pay more for clarity and strategic guidance than technical complexity; Success comes from understanding business problems and knowing where AI creates the most impact, not from technical expertise; This model provides stable recurring income through monthly partnerships

slides.title: AI CLI-Anything with Claude Code https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uzd2ckXnsg0 The video
slides.text: AI CLI-Anything with Claude Code https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Uzd2ckXnsg0 The video introduces CLI Anything, an open-source tool from Hong Kong University's Data Intelligence Labs that converts any open-source software into command-line interfaces for AI agents like Claude Code. This eliminates the need for MCP tools and provides better performance by removing the middleman between agents and programs. CLI Anything works through a seven-step automated process: analyzing code, designing, planning, testing, documenting, and publishing the CLI tool. The creator demonstrates building a CLI for draw.io from scratch, then using Claude Code to create a complex SaaS backend architecture diagram with a simple text prompt. The tool comes pre-loaded with CLIs for popular applications like Blender, Inkscape, and Audacity. The installation process is straightforward, requiring Python 3.1 and the target software, making it accessible for transforming human-designed software into agent-controllable tools. OpenClaw + PaperClip https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=49_WitY66yM PaperClip - open-source tool that integrates with OpenClaw to create entire AI-powered companies with zero human employees PaperClip creates virtual organizations with AI agents that have job titles, report to bosses, and coordinate on schedules The system features five layers: mission control for defining company goals, organizational charts with hierarchical AI roles, heartbeat scheduling for automated task completion, governance for human approval of major decisions, and multi-company management

slides.title: AI Google Gemma 4B Update! Julian Goldie SEO
slides.text: AI Google Gemma 4B Update! Julian Goldie SEO Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kQqR8BOg4Lo Google has released Translate Gemma 4B, a new AI translation model that runs entirely in web browsers without requiring internet connection, cloud servers, or data sharing. The model translates 55 languages and can even translate text within images, all while keeping data completely private on the user's device. It utilizes WebGPU technology and Transformers.js version 4 for fast performance directly in browsers. This represents a significant shift toward local AI processing, offering benefits like enhanced privacy, faster speeds, and universal access without internet dependency. The model was trained using supervised learning with human and AI-generated translations, followed by reinforcement learning optimization. Julian Goldie presents this as part of a broader trend toward browser-based, offline AI that will revolutionize how AI applications are built and used across devices. Claude Code - Code Review Claude Code’s Code Review is a multi‑agent system that automatically analyzes pull requests and local changes for logic bugs, security issues, regressions, and weak tests, while largely ignoring minor formatting. It integrates with GitHub/GitLab via an app, posting inline comments and a summary on each PR, and can also be triggered manually (for example, with @claude review). Behavior is customized using CLAUDE.md (architecture and invariants) and REVIEW.md (what to always flag or ignore), letting teams encode conventions like “no PII in logs.” Developers can also run focused, interactive reviews locally in VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, or the terminal for pre‑push checks.

slides.title: AI Canada's 200B Ops/sec Chip https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ojkStIgOcNM Canadian researchers
slides.text: AI Canada's 200B Ops/sec Chip https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ojkStIgOcNM Canadian researchers published a Nature paper claiming their cascade modulating machine achieves 200 billion operations per second at room temperature using five telecom components, reportedly outperforming D-Wave's quantum computer on certain problems. However, the reality is more nuanced.While the system uses clever photonic pulses in fiber optic loops to solve optimization problems and achieved 100% success on number partitioning tasks where D-Wave failed, it operates with only 256 spins versus competitors handling thousands to millions of variables. The "200 billion ops/sec" figure uses low-precision analog operations and is actually 18,000 times slower than an Nvidia H100 GPU at higher precision. The system also requires expensive test equipment costing hundreds of thousands of dollars. Though published in a prestigious journal, this represents more of a proof-of-concept than a breakthrough, trailing major competitors in problem size while demonstrating potential for telecom-based optimization architectures.

slides.title: AI is Killing Consulting Julia McCoy argues that
slides.text: AI is Killing Consulting Julia McCoy argues that the traditional $300-an-hour consulting industry is being rendered obsolete by advanced AI http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M8VNj21ew_4 She highlights how the core value of consulting - research, synthesis, competitive analysis, and polished communication - is now handled more efficiently by tools like Abacus AI’s Chat LLM McCoy shows in real-time demo the AI conducting market research and generating a professional, 15-slide strategic deck in just four minutes - a task that typically costs $25,000 and takes weeks for a consulting firm to complete While top-tier firms may survive by focusing on human relationships, she concludes that mid-market strategy consulting is dying Businesses adopting AI for strategic intelligence will gain a significant competitive advantage by moving faster and reducing costs Skipping the "Front Door" - Alex Karp, Palantir Current websites are designed for humans to browse and compare. AI agents will skip these "middlemen" by going directly to data and transactions via APIs Middleman sites that rely on ad impressions and affiliate clicks will "evaporate" will lose Business are shifting focus to rebuilding software to be AI-native from the ground up https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KZnuFadL7xM

slides.title: AI in Business How AI-native companies are winning
slides.text: AI in Business How AI-native companies are winning Success now depends on deciding which tasks to give to specific AI models versus human experts. AI acts as an amplifier; it improved performance for skilled entrepreneurs - but decreased it for those lacking the judgment to filter "AI slop" From Chats to Agents planning and executing Scaling with on-demand compute instead of massive headcounts Strategic focus on "earned insights", solving specific user bottlenecks with "a drop of AI" rather than over-engineering complex tools. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I08ZeY7QcrE AI Transformation - Changing Business Roles and Processes Models are good enough, but the way they are used in business is lagging . Companies are still using old processes. True productivity gains require becoming "AI-native," which involves changing team structures, skill sets, and default workflows The "RAPID 5" Framework: A strategy for transformation: Reveal (map workflows), Architect (design AI-native models), Proof (real-world pilots), Ingrain (identity shift), and Dynamize (90-day reassessment cycles) New Roles: The rise of "Forward-Deployed Engineers" at top AI labs shows that the current priority is helping customers bridge the gap between AI capability and practical use. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cglc_BR04GE

slides.title: AI in Business Julia McCoy Automated 1.2Mln/year Business
slides.text: AI in Business Julia McCoy Automated 1.2Mln/year Business https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vWXRy2_fSOc Julia McCoy built a $1.2 million business in 11 months but was working 90 hrs/week until a health crash forced her out The business continued growing and now runs on just 30 minutes of her time daily, generating over 2 Mln/mon YouTube views. She attributes this to three integrated automation systems: First, a conversion-optimized website with AI chatbots and automated SEO-focused blog content that builds authority and captures leads 24/7. Second, a custom AI copywriter trained on her voice and expertise that produces consistent content across all channels. Third, an AI clone system using tools like HeyGen and 11Labs that creates YouTube videos without filming, managed by a video editor who handles the entire content pipeline. These systems work together as a compounding flywheel, driving traffic to optimized pages while building long-term authority, allowing business owners to scale without trading time for revenue.

slides.title: AI Automating Followups Automating Followups: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4_zAMqQu6RQ Automation platform
slides.text: AI Automating Followups Automating Followups: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4_zAMqQu6RQ Automation platform N8N has 176K GitHub stars and 200K+ users Average entrepreneur wastes 16 hrs/week on repetitive tasks 1. Start with your biggest time drain (lead follow-up, invoicing, data entry) 2. Use automation as leverage, not replacement; free people to do higher-value thinking, not to eliminate jobs 3. Build systems that compound - connect automations so that lead generation feeds the CRM, which feeds follow-up, which feeds sales and reporting - one connected flow. 1. Lead Machine - a workflow that runs every morning, scrapes Google Maps for local business leads, enriches each profile with company data, uses AI to write a personalized outreach opening line, and loads everything into the CRM automatically. What used to take 5 hours now takes 4 minutes. 2. Follow-Up Engine - When a new lead enters the CRM, a 5-touch automated sequence begins: a warm intro on Day 1, a value-add on Day 3, a direct ask on Day 7, a "breakup" email on Day 14, and a final check-in on Day 21. If the lead replies at any point, the sequence stops and the owner gets a Slack notification. Every morning, a digest ranks the hottest leads by engagement signals. Follow-up consistency goes from 30–40% (manual) to 100% (automated). 3. Business Intelligence Report - Every Sunday night, a workflow pulls data from Stripe, the CRM, email tools, support tickets, and competitor monitoring, then sends it all to an AI model to produce a 400-word Monday morning briefing,  identifying what's working, what's declining, and the single most important focus for the week.

slides.title: Hallucinations in 2026 Nearly half of all executives
slides.text: Hallucinations in 2026 Nearly half of all executives admit to making major company decisions based on unchecked AI content Employees spend an average of 4 hrs/week double-checking AI output Even top academic conferences have been affected, unknowingly accepting dozens of papers containing fake, AI-generated citations A top-tier model might hallucinate 88% of the time when asked questions it doesn't know; realistic hallucination rate in normal complex conversations is approximately 30% AI models are 34% more likely to use confident language (e.g., "certainly," "definitely") at the exact moment they are providing incorrect information Grok 3 was found to fail citation accuracy 94% of the time, often providing real links but inventing the content supposedly found within them Hallucination rates vary depending on whether you are testing for "faithfulness" (summarization) or "intellectual honesty" (admitting ignorance) Claude prioritizes intellectual honesty, scoring a 0% hallucination rate on specific tests because it refuses to guess when it doesn't know an answer Gemini has a broader knowledge base but is more aggressive in fabricating answers, guessing incorrectly about half the time in similar tests GPT Models - turning on web access is the most effective way to reduce hallucinations in GPT models, plummeting the error rate from 47% to under 10% AI models are not databases; they are prediction engines designed to find the most statistically plausible next word, not the "truth" Goal Conflict - there is a fundamental trade-off between being truthful, comprehensive, and honest about limits; a model can achieve some of these goals simultaneously, but never all of them How to manage hallucinations: Tier 1 (70%+ Reduction) - use Web Search and RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) to force the AI to use specific, verified documents Tier 2 & 3 - Implement cross-checking (using one AI to check another) and specialized prompting techniques http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fHas3Dg1okk
